title: I Used the Nyckelharpa Key Log on the Mentor Who Hijacked My Numbered Keys

parts.text: I stepped into the key room at 6:09 p.m. and mentor Sigrid was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE HARPA. SIXTY MINUTES. KEYS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-nine, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered keys. Sigrid shrugged. "Mentors are the keys." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover tangents on my numbered keys. Then I asked for the key log. At 6:17 the desk pinged why Sigrid's name was on my tangents. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Sigrid's leftover tangents on my numbered keys.

social.video_title: She hijacked my numbered nyckelharpa keys — Part 1/2
social.description: Key room, leftover tangents, a sixty-minute clock she posted. I logged the keys. Would you have asked for the key log?

parts.text: Sigrid called it key dressing until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the tangent still. The keys went back to my numbered slot. Sigrid ran a slot of her own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE KEYS. I keep my keys in a labeled tray. Sigrid brown-bags her dressing. The key room finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the keys — Part 2/2
social.description: Key log, numbered keys, and a second line on the board. Was key dressing ever my tangents?
